extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners; patent owners, practitioners, and third-party reexamination requesters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding whether to merge or stay reissue applications and ex parte reexamination proceedings, and detailed procedures for conducting merged proceedings and handling concurrent litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month determination on reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination on a reexamination request must be made within three months of the request filing date (35 U.S.C. 304 and 37 CFR 1.515).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination must not be delayed because of a copending reissue application; if reexamination is ordered, CRU SPRS or TC QAS will await the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and any reply under 37 CFR 1.535 or expiration of the time for same (see MPEP §§ 2249–2251).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt notification to OPLA when concurrent filings occur
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application is filed during pendency of a reexamination (or vice versa), OPLA should be notified as promptly as possible after the application/proceeding reaches the Technology Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of the files (reexamination file, reissue application, patent file) are paper files, they should be hand-delivered to OPLA at the time of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office discretion to merge or stay proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to merge the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, or to stay one of them, is made case-by-case and is within the sole discretion of the Office to facilitate orderly operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The status of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding will be taken into account in deciding whether merger will be ordered or one proceeding stayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer merging narrower reexamination into broader reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: General Office policy is to merge the more narrow reexamination proceeding with the broader reissue application examination when desirable to expedite conduct of both proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the status of the reissue examination (e.g., not begun or not appealed to the Board tends toward merger); if the reissue application is on appeal to the Board or courts that fact weighs against merger and may support staying one proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reissue about to issue: delay determination and base reexamination on reissue claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue is expected to issue before the three-month determination for a reexamination request, the reexamination determination should normally be delayed until after granting of the reissue patent and then made based on the reissue patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is ordered, it will be on the reissue patent claims; the reexamination starting point must be presented as a 'clean copy' of the reissue claims (bracketed words from the reissue patent do not appear in the clean copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action flag when reissue issues after reexamination ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent issues after reexamination is ordered, the next examiner action should state that further proceedings will be based on the reissue patent claims and not the surrendered patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.05 may be used in the Office action to indicate proceedings are based on the reissue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for identical claims/amendments in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When merger is ordered, the patent owner must maintain identical amendments and place the same claims in the reissue application and the reexamination file for the merged proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identical amendments must be maintained for as long as proceedings remain merged (see 37 CFR 1.565(d)); if identical amendments are not present at merger, the patent owner will be required to submit a housekeeping amendment to place the same amendments in both proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housekeeping amendment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Housekeeping amendments to make claims identical across merged files may be required and must not address any issue of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housekeeping amendments are submitted under 37 CFR 1.173 in accordance with reissue practice; they can be accomplished by amending either or both proceedings as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU SPRS/TC QAS temporary jurisdiction where amendment time allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the merger decision gives the patent owner time (e.g., one month) to provide an amendment to make claims identical, the CRU SPRS or TC QAS will retain jurisdiction over the reexamination proceeding until the amendment is submitted or the time expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After amendment is received and processed or the time expires, the merged proceeding will be returned to the examiner to issue an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should advance Office action to most advanced point
rubrics_metrics.description: Once returned to the examiner for issuance of an Office action, the examiner should prepare the action at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first proceeding is ready for a final rejection and the second provides no new information requiring a new ground, the examiner should issue a final rejection for the merged proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for non-identical claims if housekeeping amendment not timely
rubrics_metrics.description: If a required housekeeping amendment to make claims identical in each file is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a rejection is because the claim would fail to particularly point out the invention due to inconsistent texts across files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merged proceeding examined under reissue practice when reissue broader
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application examination and a reexamination proceeding are merged, the merged examination will be conducted on the basis of the rules relating to the broader reissue application examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will apply reissue statute, rules, procedures, and case law to the merged proceeding; amendments should be submitted per reissue practice (37 CFR 1.121(i), 1.173; see MPEP § 1453).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Office action for merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Office action in a merged reissue/reexamination proceeding will be a single action which jointly applies to both the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each action will contain identifying data for both matters and be physically entered into both files, which remain separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single response requirement and service to requester
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant/patent owner must file a single response in a merged proceeding, filed in duplicate for entry in both files (or multiple copies if multiple reexaminations are merged), and must serve a copy on any third-party reexamination requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of all Office actions will be mailed to the third-party requester but not to any other third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic dissolution of merger for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant/patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action in a merged proceeding, the merger will be automatically dissolved and the reissue application will be held abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) will be issued and the Director will proceed to issue a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 in accordance with the last Office action, unless further action is clearly needed in view of differences between reexamination and reissue proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of express abandonment or CPA on merger
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant files an express abandonment of the reissue under 37 CFR 1.138, the merged proceeding will be dissolved and the reexamination continued; filing a CPA for a reissue design application typically dissolves the merger, stays the CPA reissue application, and continues the reexamination separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissolution based on abandonment may require the examiner to withdraw grounds not applicable under reexamination and add new grounds that are applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-dissolution handling of grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When merger is dissolved and reexamination continues, any grounds of rejection not applicable under reexamination should be withdrawn and any new grounds applicable under reexamination should be made (e.g., grounds based on improper broadened claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should note any questions remaining that cannot be considered under reexamination pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filing in reissue dissolves merger; RCE non-availability in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for continued examination (RCE) of the reissue application is filed, the merger will be automatically dissolved and the reissue application suspended; RCE practice is not available in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners are put on notice that responses in the reexamination must account for non-availability of RCE; failure to timely respond in reexamination may result in termination pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to merge/stay before reexamination order are premature
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to merge the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, or to stay one because of the other, filed before an order granting reexamination is issued will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will generally sua sponte make the decision to merge or stay; premature petitions will be expunged or returned by CRU or TC Director (see MPEP § 2267).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner can petition to merge/stay after statement filing; third-party cannot petition to merge
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or to stay at the time the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 is filed or thereafter if the Office has not acted; a third-party reexamination requester does not have standing to petition to merge a reexamination with a reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third-party requester may file a petition to stay the reexamination it requested and may file a notification of concurrent proceedings pursuant to MPEP § 2282; petitions filed after the order for reexamination will be referred to OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single fee rule in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed requiring a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension fee, petition fee, appeal/brief/oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid for the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one appeal brief fee need be paid even though copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding. Excess claim fees are governed by reissue practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedition when reexamination is court-ordered or litigation stayed
rubrics_metrics.description: When an ex parte reexamination request arises from a court order or litigation agreement (sanctioned by a court), or litigation is stayed for reexamination, all aspects of the proceeding will be expedited to the extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is ordered, examination following the patent owner’s statement (37 CFR 1.530) and requester’s reply (37 CFR 1.535) will be expedited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of federal court decisions known at determination time
rubrics_metrics.description: If a federal court decision on the patent is known to the examiner when the determination on the reexamination request is made, that decision does not automatically preclude a finding of a substantial new question (SNQ) because the Office uses different standards of proof and claim interpretation than courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-final court holdings are not controlling; final holdings of invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) are controlling and mean no SNQ exists for the claims held invalid/unenforceable. Examiner determinations after a court decision must be reviewed by CRU SPRS to ensure conformity with Office litigation policy (see MPEP § 2240).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month statutory mandate governs even when PTAB reviews exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when a PTAB review proceeding (e.g., inter partes review, post-grant review) exists for the same patent, the reexamination request must, by statute, be decided (grant or denial) within three months of its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner becomes aware of a PTAB Review Proceeding for the same patent, the ex parte reexamination must be referred to the examiner’s SPRS who will coordinate with the PTAB before taking action on the reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner litigation investigation duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must conduct a reasonable investigation to determine whether the patent under reexamination has been or is involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation includes review of the reexamination file, patent file, and litigation computer search. If litigation or a federal court decision is discovered, the examiner must notify CRU SPRS or TC QAS prior to further action so CRU SPRS/TC QAS can review actions for conformity with litigation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling court decisions that issue after reexamination ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a federal court decision issues after an ex parte reexamination is ordered (or the Office becomes aware of such a decision), the order to reexamine will be reviewed to see if an SNQ still exists; if no SNQ exists, the reexamination will be terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-final federal court decisions have no binding effect on reexamination. A final court holding of invalidity/unenforceability is binding—claims held invalid/unenforceable are withdrawn from reexamination; if all claims are finally held invalid the reexamination is vacated or terminated. Use form paragraph 22.20 to note claims held invalid by court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of NIRC and panel review at conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of an ex parte reexamination, the examiner must prepare a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) and, where appropriate, an examiner’s amendment and reasons for allowance for claims found patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner informs CRU SPRS/TC QAS of conclusion; CRU SPRS/TC QAS convene a panel review conference (see MPEP § 2271.01). If the conference confirms the examiner’s decision, an NIRC is issued and signed by the examiner with conferees initialing; if not confirmed, the examiner reevaluates and issues an appropriate Office action rejecting unconfirmed claims.
